- Can you confirm whether Redwood requires IdP-initiated SSO in addition to SP-initiated SAML?

Lena — thanks for the heads up. Looping in Marissa (Customer Success) for RBAC exports and Soojin (Product Security) for SCIM/MFA specifics.

Quick answers up front:
- SSO: Redwood supports both SP-initiated and IdP-initiated SAML flows. IdP-initiated is optional but supported for customers who require it; we document the ACS/EntityID requirements in the SAML integration guide.
- SCIM: we support group-based provisioning and deprovisioning. We offer a soft-delete window configurable per-tenant (default 30 days) and a permanent purge policy that customers can request.
- RBAC: attaching a role inventory export and a recommended least-privilege mapping (see attached CSV).
- MFA: MFA is enforced for human users accessing the console (TOTP + optional U2F). Service accounts used for non-interactive API calls are restricted by scoped API keys and short TTLs; we recommend using dedicated machine identities with scoped keys and IP allowlists. We do not force MFA on non-human service principals in the console because they should not have interactive access.

I’ve attached: saml_flow_diagram.pdf, scim_provisioning_playbook.docx, and rbac_role_inventory.csv. Marissa — can you confirm the analyst vs admin role mapping in the CSV? Soojin — can you add a short note on SCIM soft-delete retention if you want different phrasing for the SIG?

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Lena — thanks for the follow-ups. Short answers below and attaching the small evidence receipt as requested.

- Role separation: "Platform Viewer" is strictly read-only for platform telemetry, logs and billing views; it cannot modify user provisioning. "Support Analyst" can open support cases and run troubleshooting queries but cannot change RBAC or provisioning rules. Only "Platform Admin" and designated security admins can modify user provisioning or role assignments. I’ve annotated the CSV with a "sod" (separation-of-duty) column for clarity.

- SCIM deletes: we support a configurable pre-purge notification. By default we log a soft-delete and send one configurable notification to tenant admins 7 days before permanent purge; customers can change timing via the Console > Org settings or request custom retention via support.

- API key audit trails: all API-key-based activity is logged in our central audit pipeline (stored in customer-specific project buckets with 1 year retention by default). Logs include API key id, originating IP, timestamp, and filtered request metadata. Keys are tied back to a service principal id in RBAC so you can map activity to a specific machine identity. We can provide a sample log export with redacted payloads.

Attached: evidence_receipt_signed.pdf (acknowledgement), updated_rbac_role_inventory.csv (annotated), and a short export sample api_key_log_sample.json (redacted). Also linking the Drive folder with the SAML flow diagram and the SCIM playbook: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3Zephyr-SIG-evidence

If this looks good, please confirm and we’ll mark the SIG as "final for vendor review". Happy to hop on a 20-min call if Zephyr wants to walk through the RBAC mapping.
